messages:
Sam: Heads-up — I'm sketching an operator-side 'compactify + rehydrate' flow for air-gapped bundles. Idea: produce a tiny seed image + compact shard set that operators fetch via sneakernet or low-bandwidth proxies, then rehydrate on host.
Lia: Can you sketch the operator UX? what commands/steps would they run? :thinking_face:
Sam: Minimal CLI: `rictl ingest --seed seed.tar.gz --shards shards.idx` then `rictl rehydrate --target /var/lib/redwood` with streaming verification. We should support resume and partial apply.
Ben: Main risks I see: memory blowups during rehydrate (we may need to stream and patch in place), and inconsistent state if a powercut happens mid-apply.
Caroline: Also key management: we cannot delay verification until the end. Needs incremental sig verification so operator can abort on first mismatch. Otherwise partial state looks valid.
Sam: Agreed. I'm thinking of a two-phase pattern: 1) verify index & manifest signatures, 2) stream blobs and verify per-chunk signatures/merkle proofs, write into a staging area, 3) atomic swap into active path.
Lia: How big is the staging footprint? on constrained appliances we can't double the storage.
Sam: Good point. We can support two strategies: in-place patching with journaled rollback (lower extra storage, more complexity) or staging in a compact FS overlay (safer, needs ~10-20% extra). We should let operator choose via config.
Ben: For in-place with journal, we need a clear crash-consistency model. Suggest we reuse operator's existing transactional apply op (like kubernetes' atomic dir swap) and emit a short failure path for half-applied artifacts.
Caroline: Rollback UX matters. Operators will want a single `rictl rollback --to vX` that can revert even if activation failed midway. That argues for keeping previous layout around until successful swap.
Sam: Right. So we land new files to `.next/` and on success swap symlinks; fallback clears `.next/`. For extremely space constrained devices, we can offer chunked patching with a small bitmap that records applied chunks — allows resume without full copy.
Lia: Networking: how do we handle mirrors/proxies? want to allow store-and-forward appliances that resume downloads without re-auth.
Sam: Design: shards are content-addressed gzip chunks. We include a small resume index with byte ranges and per-chunk hash+sig; operators can request ranges from nearby mirror. Resume index is signed.
Ben: Security: need to ensure signature coverage extends to the resume index and any mutating metadata. Also consider timestamp/epoch rotation so old shims can't replay newer manifests.
Caroline: Epoch rotation raises operator friction. We should provide clear migration tooling: `rictl trust rotate --old-epoch X --new-key /path/to/key` and dry-run mode.
Sam: Performance: rehydrate should be parallel but bounded (configurable concurrency). For GPUs and model shards we should prefer streaming KV-cache-friendly layout to avoid memory spikes.
Lia: Observability: operators will ask 'how far along is rehydrate' — expose per-shard progress and verification status in Console and CLI. Add checkpoint hooks for automated monitoring to scrape.
Ben: Also surface a compact integrity report: list of failed chunks + hashes so operator can request exactly the bad ranges from a mirror.
Caroline: Failure modes: corrupted shard, missing shard, signature mismatch, out-of-disk. For each we need deterministic operator guidance and a recommended remediation (eg, fetch from proxy, increase disk, revert).
Sam: I'm drafting an RFC with sections: flow diagram, failure modes + playbooks, operator CLI, on-disk layout, signature model (index+chunk-level sigs), and tests. Quick design questions: do we require content-level merkle proofs or is chunk-level signature enough?
Lia: Chunk-level sigs are simpler and smaller. Merkle proofs add flexibility for partial fetch but increase complexity on signers. Might be overkill for v1.
Ben: Agree start with per-chunk signatures + signed resume index. Add merkle in v2 if we need dedupe across bundles.
Caroline: One more thing: automation for secure rollback lifecycle. If an activation fails repeatedly, we should mark the bundle as tainted and require manual intervention. Avoid automatic continual retries that can brick devices.
Sam: Great note. I'll add a 'taint' state and operator notification rule.
deploy-bot: canary: compactify-operator-flow RFC draft deployed to staging at 1789994450 :rocket:
Sam: Thanks. I'll post a link to the draft RFC once it's up. Looking for :eyes: on the crash-consistency and signature coverage sections.
Lia: I'll review those sections tomorrow. Ben/Caroline if you can sanity-check rollback and storage-footprint numbers that'd be great.
Ben: Will do. Quick Q: any constraints for on-prem HSMs?
Sam: We'll support external KMS via PKCS11 and a local offline signing tool for airgap keys. Document expected operator steps for key escrow.
Caroline: Sounds good. If we keep the operator flow small and scriptable (`rictl` commands) we can then add operator-UI wizards later.
Sam: Cool. I'll upload RFC link in ~1h. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
